title: Deep Learning Enhancements of 4DSTEM Ptychographic Reconstruction
content: Ptychography has emerged as one of the most powerful phase retrieval methods in four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4DSTEM), offering high-resolution, dose-efficient imaging for a range of materials [1]. By solving for both the object and probe wavefunctions, ptychographic reconstructions achieve super-resolution imaging, aberration correction, and dose-efficient phase contrast. These are all critical for characterizing beam-sensitive and weakly scattering materials. Multislice ptychography extends this approach to strongly scattering materials, partitioning the object into thin slices along the beam direction and solving for depth-dependent phase variations [2]. This enables 3D structure reconstruction without requiring a tilt series, making it particularly useful characterizing beam-sensitive nanostructures, defects, and strain fields.
